quest.title: Captain Comet's Lost Treasure
quest.hook: Captain Comet hid her treasure across 5 islands. Solve each clue, then beat the Fraction Kraken!

intro.title: Phishing Lagoon
intro.story: Sneaky pirates fish for passwords here. Spot their tricks and sail on!

questions.prompt: Quick one! Which message is phishing?
questions.hint: Who would ever need your password?
questions.explanation: Real friends and companies never ask for your password. That one is a phishing trick.

questions.prompt: Speed round! Is it SAFE online?
statements: Click a prize link from a stranger.
Tell a grown-up about a weird message.
Share your password with a new friend.
questions.hint: Passwords stay secret. Strangers with prizes are a red flag.
questions.explanation: Keep passwords secret, skip stranger links, and tell a grown-up.

intro.title: Simile Swamp
intro.story: The swamp guard only talks in similes and metaphors. Learn the trick to pass!

questions.title: The 'like or as' trick
questions.body: A simile compares with LIKE or AS. A metaphor says one thing IS another. Look for like or as!

questions.prompt: A simile uses the word like or ___.
steps: Look for the little word LIKE or AS.
Found it? Then it's a simile!

questions.prompt: Match each sentence to its type!
questions.hint: Look for like or as first.
questions.explanation: "As" and "like" make similes. "Time is money" is a metaphor.

questions.prompt: Finish the simile: The pirate was as brave as a ___.
questions.hint: Any brave animal or hero works. Just one or two words!
questions.explanation: Lions are famous for being brave, so we say brave as a lion!
questions.celebrate: Nice! A lion is a classic, but "{given}" works too! 🦁

questions.title: Songs love similes
questions.body: Tons of songs use similes, like "shine bright like a diamond." Listen for them today!

intro.title: Who-Which Bridge
intro.story: The bridge troll loves extra info. Add it with who, which, or that to cross!

questions.title: Who, which, that
questions.body: A relative clause adds extra info about a noun. Use WHO for people, WHICH or THAT for things.

steps: Is it a person or a thing?

questions.prompt: My friend, ___ loves pizza, ate three slices.
questions.hint: Is a friend a person or a thing?
questions.explanation: A friend is a person, so it's who.

questions.prompt: Match each start to its ending!
questions.hint: Wooden leg? Green wings? Full of gold? Who has which?
questions.explanation: The pirate has a wooden leg, the parrot flaps green wings, the chest is full of gold!

intro.title: Starlight Lookout
intro.story: Captain Comet steers by the stars. Why do some look brighter?

questions.title: Closer looks brighter
questions.body: A flashlight looks brighter up close. The Sun is just a star that's REALLY close to you!

template.note: The Sun is a star. Other stars are way farther.

statements: The Sun is the biggest star.
questions.hint: The Sun only looks big because it's close.
questions.explanation: The Sun is a medium star. Distance changes how bright stars look.
steps: Think: is the star close or far?

intro.title: Fraction Training Cove
intro.story: The Kraken loves fraction riddles. Train here first!

questions.title: "Of" means times
questions.body: 1/2 of 1/4 means 1/2 × 1/4. Multiply the tops, then multiply the bottoms.

questions.explanation: Cut the half into 3 equal parts: each part is 1/6 of the whole. Multiply both bottoms, 3 × 2 = 6. No common denominator needed.

feedback.1/2: Careful! Times is not like adding. Multiply the bottoms too: 3 × 2.
feedback.2/5: That adds tops and bottoms. For times, multiply them instead.

intro.title: The Fraction Kraken!
intro.story: The Kraken guards the treasure. Hit it with fraction power 3 times in a row!

questions.prompt: Shade 1/2 of 3/4 of the bar! (Hint: 8 parts)
questions.hint: 3/4 is 6 parts. Half of 6 parts is…

questions.prompt: You eat 2/3 of half a pizza. What fraction is that?
The map says walk 3/4 mile, 4 times. How far?

questions.explanation: Half of a quarter is a smaller piece: 2 × 4 = 8 parts, so 1/8. Treasure unlocked!

feedback.1/4: Ooh, the bottom stayed 4. Half of a quarter is smaller, so multiply: 2 × 4.
feedback.1/6: That adds 2 + 4. For times, multiply the bottoms.

topics.powerup: Boss ahead! Remember: "of" means times. Multiply the tops, then the bottoms.

Kraken.d: A giant sea monster from old sailor stories.

captain.d: The leader of a ship and its crew.

relative clause.d: Extra info about a noun, starting with who, which or that.

troll.d: A grumpy creature from fairy tales who guards bridges.
